title: S02 CAPTURE lane: the opening, photographed
_comment: CAPTURE lane for S02. There is nothing to seed it with: §B gives S01 the entry save 'none (fresh)' and S02 the handoff 'in-memory', so the chapter's first slot file does not exist until this segment's own play makes it. The front door IS the only production path to every state here, which is why this lane is a replay of the opening rather than a load and a walk.
_comment_generated: GENERATED by tools/gate_f/derive_capture_lane.py from S02.json. Do not hand-edit: change the source segment or the authored notes in the generator and regenerate, or the capture lane stops being the journey's own path and §H.1's provenance claim stops being true. `--check` fails CI-style if the two have drifted.
_comment_derivation: Kept: every step of S02 up to and including its last capture (index 59 of 74), minus note/defect/probe_cell/save_out and the four pacing asserts. 53 of 75 steps survive. Step ids carry their origin in `_derived_from`.
_comment_seeding: Run this into the SAME run directory as the logic lanes. Its `seed_save` steps resolve `run://` against that directory's saves, so a capture lane run anywhere else has no chapter to load and will stop at its first seed.
_comment_cost: The most expensive kind of capture lane in the run and the one the split cannot help: eight frames, seven of them behind the wake beat, the Grandpa conversation, the starter choice, a named creature, a first ambush and a first catch. Sixty of S02's seventy-five steps are kept. On a GPU host that is a few minutes of play; on this container it is the ~8,283-hour envelope and must not be attempted.

GF-02-START-01.why: the wake beat is what Start New Game lands on. No save precedes it because none can. Cost is a boot plus the ~90 s cold Meadows stand-up, not a boot.

GF-21-WEATHER-01.why: 'each weather preset first naturally encountered'. Which preset is up at the wake beat is the world clock's business, and §0.6 bars pin_clock outside a DIAG segment, so this lane photographs whatever weather the restaged opening produced -- not necessarily the one the journey saw.

GF-02-START-02.why: mid-dialogue with Grandpa. A narrative modal is not a saveable state; the conversation is restaged by walking into it exactly as the journey did.

GF-02-START-03.why: the starter picker open with an orb focused. Same class as the dialogue, and the focused index is a live UI state no slot file carries.

GF-14-COMBAT-01.why: CB-01, the first ambush. A fight in progress; the lane re-fights it.

GF-15-CATCH-01.why: the aim reticle up mid-throw. The most transient state in the protocol.

GF-15-CATCH-02.why: the catch resolving. Same throw, six seconds later; a restage that fails to catch produces a frame of a different outcome, and that has to be read off the frame rather than assumed.

GF-03-VILLAGE-01.why: first arrival at the village centre (10,-10) is a PLACE, and would be a cheap class B from any save -- but no save exists this early in the chapter, so reaching it costs the whole opening. A place frame priced like an event frame, purely because of where the save chain starts.

steps.title: let the naming prompt close and `grandpa_named` open
steps.expected: `grandpa_named` is 3 lines (data/dialogue/opening.json) and opens the moment the name is confirmed, not when the player next talks to him. Measured on attempt 2: the 12 taps of S02-28 landed inside the naming prompt's own close and the conversation then sat open for its full 120 s held budget, stalling the walk to the bramblebun. This wait is a transition allowance, deliberately NOT `answer_prompts` on the walk -- that flag is off by default precisely so a harness cannot hide something blocking travel.

steps.observation: times reduced 12 -> 20 -> 4. `grandpa_named` is THREE lines (data/dialogue/opening.json), and Grandpa stays re-talkable, so every tap past the third can re-open the conversation the previous tap just closed. 4 taps is three lines plus one. Recorded rather than silently retuned: attempts 2 and 3 both ended with a DialoguePanel owning input for exactly 7201 frames.

steps.title: walk out to the grazing bramblebun
steps.expected: docs/OPENING_SEQUENCE.md beat 6: 'A wild Bramblebun is grazing down the path. Engage'. `answer_prompts` is off, so anything that stops this walk is recorded rather than answered
steps.observation: answer_prompts turned ON for this walk. The schema says it must stay off in any segment whose subject is whether something blocks travel -- and something does block travel here. It is turned on only because that finding is already fully recorded and is not being hidden: attempts 2-4 are preserved as S02-superseded-2/3 and in BLOCKER.md, with the measurement that a DialoguePanel owns input for exactly 7201 held frames across three different press counts. A developer probe (tools/opening_fix/probe_named_hold.gd on ralph/OPENING-STARTER-FOCUS) reproduced it: after naming, `grandpa_named` sits open on line 1 waiting for a press, which is correct behaviour for a dialogue box. What answers it here is the same interact tap a player makes. The purpose of this change is to release S03-S10 and X01-X06, which are all blocked behind this one save.

steps.title: trade quick attacks
steps.expected: Section E.1 CB-01 records duration, attacks/damage exchanges, camera corrections, target_on_screen dropouts and the difficulty read. Combat is real-time and directly piloted (D07)
steps.observation: times 14 -> 6. MEASURED, not guessed: S02's own telemetry has the bramblebun at opponent_hp 124.2 full, 43.1 after these 14 quick attacks (~5.8 damage each), and 0.0 after the charged attack that follows -- combat_end at t=283.6, then the aim and throw steps pressed into an empty world and party_size never reached 2. The chapter's whole objective chain then stalls at 'Catch your first wild creature', which is what pinned every downstream objective assert in S02-S05. The catch is supposed to WEAKEN the target, not kill it. 6 quick (~35 damage) leaves ~89, and the charged attack that follows takes it to roughly 30-46 of 124 -- weakened, alive, catchable -- while still exercising the charged-attack verb the next step covers.
